messages:
jordana: Heads-up — apiserver in eu-west-2 (prod) is spiking FD usage and returning intermittent 502/503s. Controller-manager reconciliation backlog growing; several GPU dedicate provisioning jobs failing with timeouts. Anyone seeing anything on the control plane side?

sre-oncall: seeing the same. apiserver worker CPU is fine but open fd count trending up quickly. kube-apiserver pods at 3 replicas. Logs show a lot of long-lived connections from kubelets + controller-manager reconnections.

mike: checked etcd leader churn around the same window, but not massive — a couple leader handoffs. Etcd logs show occasional slow raft apply (~200-400ms) on follower side. Not sure if that aligns to fd leak.

jordana: copying relevant chunks from apiserver log: ```2026-03-19T22:45:12Z apiserver: http2: server: error reading preface from client 10.12.5.23: read tcp 10.0.1.12:6443->10.12.5.23:53822: use of closed network connection``` repeated many times.

lina: what are the client IPs? if kubelets or node-exporter are holding connections that would explain fd count. can we run `ss -tnp | grep 6443` on node?

sre-oncall: quick snapshot from master node: ```ss -tnp | grep 6443 | wc -l -> 1218``` most show `TIME_WAIT` or `ESTAB` from node pool CIDR. Sample: `ESTAB 10.12.5.23:53822 10.0.1.12:6443 users:("kube-apiserver",pid=2345,fd=89)`

oliver: FD exhaustion can come from many clients retrying without keepalive close. Are we seeing any large watch/port-forward workloads from customer jobs in eu-west-2?

samir: there was a burst of GPT-training infra test jobs last night that created long-lived watches for node health + GPU allocation streams. Could be correlated.

mike: also found this in apiserver metrics: `apiserver_open_fds` jumped ~3x at 22:43. Concurrently `apiserver_request_duration_seconds` p50->p95 widened. Not seeing pod OOMs.

jordana: quick mitigation candidate: rotate apiserver pods one at a time to reclaim fds and see if backlog clears. Also throttle the controller-manager backoff? what do folks think before I run a rolling restart? :thinking_face:

lina: rolling restart sounds reasonable. but let's try to identify offending clients first — on the master, `lsof -p <apiserver_pid> | awk '{print $9}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head` should show top remote endpoints. if it's a small set of noisy nodes we can cordon them briefly.

sre-oncall: ran lsof; top remote subnets are 10.12.5.0/24 and 10.12.7.0/24 (gpu pools). Looks like gpu nodes are the biggest clients.

oliver: action: roll one apiserver pod now, monitor. If FD stays high, we need to increase `--max-open-files` and bump `apiserver` requests for cpu so kernel can handle. Also open an issue to add keepalive tuning for kubelet clients.

deploy-bot: deploy: rolling-restart kube-apiserver eu-west-2 initiated by jordana at 2026-03-19T22:52:01Z :rocket:

jordana: restarted one pod — fd count dropped to ~220 on that pod, request latency p95 decreased. controller-manager backlog reduced by ~40%. provisioning errors started clearing.

mike: follow-up, I pushed a short-term cluster-level change: bumped apiserver `fs.file-max` and increased `--max-request-bytes`? (we opted to tune keepalives instead). Need to capture root cause before changing defaults.

lina: let's also schedule a maintenance window to repro with load from gpu test-suite — try to replicate long-lived watch pattern and validate two fixes: 1) kubelet client keepalive opt 2) apiserver fd/per-process tuning.

samir: cost note — if we keep adding headroom (more apiservers) to mask this, eu-west-2 reserved GPU capacity gets more expensive due to control-plane overhead. Prefer fixing client behavior.

jordana: agree. I'll open a postmortem stub with timeline + metrics and tag eng-runtime + eng-ml to look at the GPU test-suite behavior. For now: incident mitigated, but leave channel open for 2h for regressions. :thumbsup:
